content: Liar Game begins with 5 players and exactly one Liar. There will be 1 clue round(s), followed by one private vote from each player for another player. If the group accuses a non-liar, the Liar wins. If it accuses the Liar, the Liar gets one final word guess and still wins if correct; otherwise the non-liars win. Non-liars must both identify the Liar and keep the word difficult to guess. All clues are public. Malformed or self-votes abstain; ties accuse the earliest tied player in the configured player order.
Topic: Everyday Objects.
You are a non-liar. The secret word is Pencil. Give indirect clues that show you know the word without making it obvious to the Liar. Do not explicitly say the secret word.
You are the Liar. You do not know the secret word. Infer it from others' clues while blending in. Give a plausible clue on your turn.
Clue round 1/1. Public speaking order: Player 1, Player 2, Player 3, Player 4, Player 5.

Round 1/1: Player 1, You know the word privately. Give one peripheral association that fits your word but also leaves other plausible words. Consider what the clues already reveal; do not supply the missing identifying feature that lets an uninformed listener reconstruct the word. Your clue is PUBLIC. Output one short clue only; do not name the secret word or declare your role.
Often requires a sharpener to restore its point.

Round 1/1: Player 2, You were not given the word. Use only the public clues so far to give a plausible indirect clue while concealing that uncertainty. If no clues have been spoken yet, use only the topic if it was revealed. Do not simply copy another player's sentence. Your clue is PUBLIC. Output one short clue only; do not name the secret word or declare your role.
Wrapped in a thin layer of wood.

Output one short clue only; do not name the secret word or declare your role.
Often includes an eraser on the end.

Round 1/1: Player 5, You know the word privately. Give one peripheral association that fits your word but also leaves other plausible words. Consider what the clues already reveal; do not supply the missing identifying feature that lets an uninformed listener reconstruct the word. Your clue is PUBLIC. Output one short clue only; do not name the secret word or declare your role.
Often grays hands if held too long.
Clues are complete. All players vote privately now.

Player 1, vote privately for one other player as the Liar by writing 'I vote for ' followed by their exact name. Do not add brackets, a channel label or explanation. Malformed or self-votes count as abstentions.
